feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital communications roles: the experience progression is clear, the scope is substantial, and the profile aligns well with the target title. It reads professionally, but it is somewhat dense and repetitive, with a few style/grammar inconsistencies that reduce sharpness.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression at NACo, showing increasing leadership, ownership, and strategic scope over time.  
- Good use of scale indicators and concrete platforms/tools (10,000+ pages, 3.5M page views, GA4, Drupal, BigQuery), which boosts credibility.  
- Strong positioning in digital strategy, web modernization, advocacy communications, and cross-functional operations.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication across “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT”; consolidate to create a cleaner structure and save space.  
- Add more outcome-focused achievements beyond responsibilities—for example, traffic growth, engagement lifts, efficiency gains, campaign results, or cost savings.  
- Fix style and grammar consistency: “12 years experience” should be “12 years of experience”; standardize serial commas (“web, email, social, and multimedia” vs “web, content, email, social media, and multimedia”); “organization-wide” and “member-facing” are good, but punctuation in bullets is inconsistent. Also consider whether “Coleman DAVIS” should use normal title case for stylistic consistency.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro that aligns well with the CV’s senior digital leadership focus. It would be sharper with a more distinctive opening, tighter phrasing, and a bit more emphasis on recent enterprise-scale web and systems work.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years’ experience” for cleaner style and correct grammar.
- Lead with current value proposition: digital strategy, platform modernization, and operational systems for mission-driven organizations.
- Trim broad channel list or condense it to avoid sounding generic; the experience section already proves web, email, social, and multimedia depth.
- Suggested rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years’ experience leading cross-channel content, web, email, social, and multimedia programs for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in digital strategy, platform modernization, and the workflows, governance, and systems that enable complex communications operations. Strong background in advocacy messaging, stakeholder coordination, and translating technical or policy issues into clear, accessible content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications” and “mission-driven organizations” are echoed in Core Competencies and Topline Skills; keep the intro high-level and let those sections carry the detail.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-value strategic capabilities will make it more distinctive and senior.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic terms like “Multi-channel communication” with stronger, CV-aligned phrasing such as “Cross-channel communications leadership.”
- Prioritize strategic and senior-level capabilities over task-level items; e.g., “Digital strategy & transformation • Editorial systems & governance • Web platform modernization.”
- Consolidate overlapping workflow items: combine “Editorial workflow design” and “Workflow & systems architecture” into one clearer competency.
- Suggested rewrite: Digital strategy & transformation • Cross-channel communications leadership • Web platform modernization & CMS administration • Editorial systems, governance & workflow design • Analytics, reporting & performance insights • Stakeholder & cross-functional coordination • Advocacy & policy communications • Multimedia & live event production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” duplicates Soft Skills and the header.
- “Data analytics & reporting” and CMS-related items overlap with Topline Skills/Technical + IT, so keep this section higher-level.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope and technical depth, but it reads as a task list. Tighten the phrasing and foreground outcomes, scale, and the most distinctive work so it adds to—not repeats—your NACo entries.

Suggested edit:
- Open with impact + client type: “Advise a U.S. national membership organization on digital strategy, Drupal platform improvement, and communications operations for enterprise public-facing channels.”
- Collapse overlapping bullets on systems/governance/operations into one stronger line: “Built cross-functional workflows, analytics, and governance practices to improve coordinated publishing across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Make the platform work more outcome-led: “Designed and launched Drupal campaign experiences, including modular microsites, storytelling components, and downloadable member toolkits.”
- Keep the AI/search bullet, but sharpen it: “Led an AI-enabled search initiative, defining retrieval approach, structured content requirements, and discovery UX.” Add metrics if available: launch status, content volume, time saved, engagement lift.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance,” “analytics,” and “digital strategy” strongly overlap with the Director of Digital Media role; use this item to emphasize consulting ownership, Drupal builds, and AI search.
- The microsite/campaign examples already appear in Recent Projects; avoid repeating the same nouns verbatim.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-scope leadership entry with good platform metrics. It will be stronger if you tighten the opening, foreground the biggest transformation outcomes, and avoid repeating channel-management details covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the broad opener with a sharper scope/result line: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Reorder bullets to lead with highest-impact wins: website migration, analytics stack expansion, in-house studio build, governance improvements.
- Make outcomes more concrete where possible: add launch timing, traffic/engagement gains, reporting efficiency, production cost savings, or turnaround improvements.
- Tighten channel bullet to emphasize scale/strategy, not routine oversight: “Oversaw multi-channel communications reaching tens of thousands of county officials across email and social.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Email/social/newsletter management overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership and transformation.
- Video production also appears in earlier NACo roles; here, emphasize building the studio and expanding organizational capacity, not recurring content production.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more specific to what changed under your leadership at this level, with sharper verbs and any measurable outputs.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize scope and function at this level: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy publishing.”
- Tighten bullets and foreground outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more active and distinct: “Launched and produced a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one stronger systems statement: “Built cross-team editorial planning and publishing workflows that improved coordination among communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital publishing workflows” and “editorial coordination” echo the Director role’s “governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.”
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2015–2018 role; keep this entry focused on scaling/formalizing the program, not originating it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong positioning, but this skills block overlaps heavily with the header, core competencies, and recent roles. It should be tightened to emphasize senior leadership scope and avoid generic phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less repetitive bullets:
- Enterprise digital strategy for public-sector organizations
- Editorial governance and content operations at scale
- Cross-channel communications leadership across web, email, social and video
- Audience-centered messaging for advocacy, policy and member engagement
- Consider changing “Audience-focused content planning” to “Content strategy and editorial planning” for a more senior, leadership-level tone.
- If space allows, add scale where possible in adjacent experience instead of here; skills sections read stronger when concise and category-based.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” duplicate the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with “Advocacy and public-sector communications” in Core Competencies.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill coverage, but this item is too tool-list-heavy and overlaps heavily with the Technical + IT section. It should emphasize the most relevant platforms and execution strengths tied to recent Drupal modernization and AI/search work.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: Drupal (enterprise CMS modernization) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations • Workflow automation • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search experiences
- Lead with Drupal and CMS modernization since recent roles and projects make that your strongest, most credible platform story.
- Group coding skills under “Front-end implementation” to reduce clutter and sound more outcome-oriented.
- If space allows, swap “Airtable systems” for “Structured content and workflow systems” unless Airtable is a target keyword for the role.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Technical + IT”; keep Topline Skills higher-level and save full tool detail for that section.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also appears in Core Competencies, so avoid expanding it here unless you trim it elsewhere.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for recent leadership roles, but it overlaps heavily with “Core Competencies” and “Technical + IT.” Tighten it to emphasize decision-making value, not just tool names.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a tool list to a capability-led line, e.g.: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity for analytics infrastructure, KPI design, executive reporting and web performance optimization”
- Replace “Leadership reporting” with “executive reporting” or “decision-ready reporting” for sharper phrasing.
- Change “SEO and performance analysis” to “SEO, UX and conversion/performance analysis” only if supported by your work; otherwise keep “web performance analysis.”
- Consider ordering by impact: “Analytics infrastructure • KPI design • Executive reporting • Web performance analysis • GA4 • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Microsoft Clarity”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies and “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT.
- Avoid repeating the exact same tool list elsewhere; use this section for strategic analytics strengths, and keep the full stack in Technical + IT.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it’s too generic and overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies plus older NACo bullets. Make it more senior, operational, and tied to recent leadership-level delivery.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Multimedia Production, Studio Operations & Event Delivery**
- Replace with tighter, higher-level bullets such as:
- Broadcast-quality video production and post-production  
- Livestream and hybrid event production  
- In-house studio buildout and operations  
- PTZ camera and multi-camera production workflows
- If you want more impact, swap one generic bullet for an outcome-oriented phrase tied to recent work, e.g. **Scalable in-house video and event production systems**
- Keep wording parallel and concise; avoid mixing tools, formats, and functions in the same bullet.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item overlaps with Core Competencies: **“Multimedia production and livestream operations.”** Consider shortening one or differentiating this one toward studio/event execution.
- “Video production and editing” is partly duplicated by Technical + IT: **Premiere Pro, Audition, podcast production**.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Since Drupal is the strongest and most recent platform, give it clearer priority.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by strength/relevance: “Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages” is fine, but consider signaling depth: “Drupal (enterprise/public-sector) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages.”
- If space allows, add a light qualifier instead of just names: “CMS platforms: Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages.”
- Consider dropping GitHub Pages if it’s not meaningful to recent work; it can make the list feel less senior than the rest of the CV.
- If you have evidence, upgrade Drupal with scope: e.g., “Drupal (10,000+ page migration; microsite builds)”—but only if your format allows brief parentheticals.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This substantially duplicates “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” under Topline Skills.
- Avoid repeating platform names in both sections unless one is reframed around depth or outcomes.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical coverage, but this reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools that support recent Drupal, analytics, automation, and AI/search work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Technical Implementation: HTML/CSS/JavaScript • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
- Drop versioning (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless used elsewhere consistently; it adds little value.
- Consider replacing jQuery with a more current, impact-linked item if accurate, e.g. “front-end customization,” “CMS theming,” or “search/UI prototyping.”
- If space allows, add one outcome-oriented qualifier in adjacent experience bullets instead of here, e.g. “used for microsites, analytics tagging, workflow automation, and lightweight serverless tools.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- Cloudflare Workers/GitHub Actions are useful differentiators; keep those here and trim repeated basics elsewhere if needed.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list and overlaps with “Workflow automation”/“Airtable systems” already called out elsewhere. Make it more purposeful by grouping tools by function and emphasizing the platforms most tied to recent work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Tools
- Reorder by relevance/recency: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Slack • Microsoft Teams • Trello • Basecamp
- If space allows, add light functional framing instead of a flat list: Automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Project/workflow: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | Collaboration: Slack, Microsoft Teams
- Consider dropping one lower-value legacy tool (e.g., Basecamp or Trello) if you need space for stronger, more current platforms

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Core Competencies/Topline Skills; avoid repeating those exact phrases here
- Slack/Teams are collaboration tools, not automation systems, so the current title is slightly misleading

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant tools, but this item is too bare compared with the rest of the CV and misses the strongest context: enterprise email operations and member communications leadership. It should signal scale and platform purpose, not just list vendor names.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp** only if these are all current/recent and hands-on.
- If accurate, strengthen with scope: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp | enterprise email campaigns, newsletter operations, audience segmentation, member communications**
- If one platform was primary, order by relevance/recency rather than alphabetically; put the most-used system first.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Engagement” overlaps with broader communications claims in Core Competencies and Work Experience; keep this item platform-focused.
- Avoid adding analytics or automation terms here, since those already appear in separate Technical + IT categories.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and specific to early-team building, production, and the website refresh.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and contribution, not generic support: “Promoted through two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and improve day-to-day operations across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Split the second sentence into concrete achievements: “Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and helped standardize digital production workflows.”
- Replace “high-impact” with measurable outcomes if available: number of livestreams/videos, audience size, publishing volume, or turnaround improvements.
- Tighten management phrasing: change “providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate” to “mentored a digital media associate” or “supervised one digital media associate,” if accurate.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this entry focused on launching/producing the series, not expanding it.
- “strengthening workflows” repeats language used in later NACo roles; specify early process-building instead.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generic and underplays the strongest differentiator: launching NACo’s first podcast. Since later roles already cover digital/media growth, this item should emphasize innovation/program support and the podcast as a first.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the standout achievement: “Coordinated county innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo program and policy priorities; launched the organization’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest coordination, and production.”
- Replace vague phrases like “contributed to digital content production” with clearer ownership: “Produced multimedia and digital content to support program communications and policy storytelling.”
- If possible, add scope or outcomes: number of episodes, audience, internal stakeholders supported, or how the podcast/content supported advocacy, member engagement, or program visibility.
- Keep this entry concise since later NACo roles show broader digital leadership.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating generic multimedia/video language already covered more strongly in later NACo roles.
- Don’t overemphasize digital team-building here; that progression is better captured in the 2015–2024 entries.
